tagline: The spiritual and historic heart of Asian Istanbul — ferry landings, Ottoman mosques, tea gardens, and one of the city's most beloved waterfront promenades.

items.name: Çamlıca Çay Bahçesi
items.description: A sprawling tea garden on the slopes of Büyük Çamlıca hill with panoramic views of the entire Bosphorus and Istanbul. One of the city's great viewpoints.
items.tip: Go on a clear day for views spanning both continents. Sunset is spectacular but busy — weekday afternoons are more peaceful.

items.name: İskele Çay Bahçeleri
items.description: Traditional tea gardens right by the Üsküdar ferry landing. Watching ferries cross the Bosphorus over a glass of çay is a perfect Istanbul moment.

items.name: Kuzguncuk Kahveleri
items.description: The charming neighbourhood of Kuzguncuk (just north of Üsküdar) has excellent independent cafés on its picturesque main street.

items.name: Kanaat Lokantası
items.description: A historic Istanbul lokanta open since 1933. Traditional home-style Turkish cooking in a timeless setting. One of the best of its kind in the city.
items.tip: Arrive at noon when the daily dishes are freshest. The braised lamb and stuffed vegetables are outstanding.

items.name: Üsküdar Balık Restoranları
items.description: Several excellent fish restaurants near the Üsküdar waterfront. Better value than European side equivalents with the same quality.

items.name: Kuzguncuk Kasabı (Butcher Meyhane)
items.description: The Kuzguncuk neighbourhood has a cluster of excellent meyhane (tavern-restaurants) popular with locals. Mezes and grilled meat in a relaxed garden setting.

items.name: Üsküdar Waterfront Promenade
items.description: A beautiful long waterfront walk with unmatched views of the Bosphorus, Topkapı Palace, and the old city skyline. One of Istanbul's finest urban walks.
items.tip: Walk north toward Kuzguncuk at dusk for the best light on the European shore skyline. About 30 minutes each way.

items.name: Büyük Çamlıca Mosque
items.description: Istanbul's newest and largest mosque, visible from across the city. The interior is vast and the hilltop location offers extraordinary views.

items.name: Kuzguncuk
items.description: A remarkably preserved historic neighbourhood with wooden Ottoman houses, colourful façades, a Greek church, synagogue, and mosque on the same street.
items.tip: Walk up the main street (İcadiye Cad.) on a Sunday morning. The neighbourhood is quiet, beautiful, and feels like it belongs to another era.

items.name: Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi)
items.description: The iconic tower in the Bosphorus — a short boat ride from Üsküdar. Newly restored with a café and restaurant inside.
items.tip: Book the restaurant for dinner to avoid the entrance queue. The exterior is best photographed from Üsküdar waterfront at golden hour.

tips: Üsküdar is reached by ferry from Eminönü (15 min) or Beşiktaş (10 min) — the ferry journey itself is part of the experience.
Also accessible by metro (Üsküdar station on the M5 line) and Marmaray rail under the Bosphorus.
Kuzguncuk is a 20-minute walk north along the waterfront from the ferry landing — highly recommended.
One of the most authentic and least-touristed major neighbourhoods in Istanbul. Deeply local in character.
